definition: Anyone affected by a project or decision, inside or outside the company.
business_context_example: Every stakeholder gets the summary, not the 40-page report.

definition: The group of senior people who govern a company.
business_context_example: The board of directors meets four times a year.

definition: The main office of an organisation.
business_context_example: Headquarters is in Munich, but most staff work remotely.

definition: A diagram showing who reports to whom in a company.
business_context_example: After the merger, nobody could read the org chart.

definition: The person you report to directly.
business_context_example: Ask your line manager to approve the training budget.

definition: An employee who reports to you.
business_context_example: She has six direct reports and two open positions.

definition: To change how a company is organised.
business_context_example: They restructured the sales team into three regions.

definition: To reduce the number of employees.
business_context_example: The plant downsized from 400 workers to 260.

definition: The number of people employed.
business_context_example: Headcount is frozen until the new budget is approved.

definition: To pay another company to do work you used to do yourself.
business_context_example: We outsource payroll but keep recruitment in house.

definition: Done inside the company by your own staff.
business_context_example: The training is delivered in house by two senior teachers.

definition: Two companies joining to become one.
business_context_example: The merger doubled our client base overnight.

definition: One company buying another.
business_context_example: The acquisition closes in March if the regulators agree.

definition: The percentage of a market that a company controls.
business_context_example: We gained 4% market share without lowering prices.

definition: What makes a company better than its rivals.
business_context_example: Our competitive advantage is speed, not price.

definition: A written argument explaining why a project is worth doing.
business_context_example: Write a one-page business case before you ask for the money.

definition: A plan showing the main steps and timing of a project.
business_context_example: The roadmap puts the mobile app in Q3, not Q2.

definition: An important point or achievement in a project plan.
business_context_example: The first milestone is 50 users by the end of May.

definition: A specific result a project must produce.
business_context_example: The deliverable is a 20-page report, not a conversation.

definition: The agreed limits of what a project includes.
business_context_example: Translation is outside the scope of this contract.

definition: When a project slowly grows beyond what was agreed.
business_context_example: Three 'small extras' later, that's scope creep.

definition: Key performance indicator: a number used to measure success.
business_context_example: Our main KPI this year is student retention, not sign-ups.

definition: A standard used for comparison.
business_context_example: We use the industry benchmark of 70% attendance.

definition: A result you aim to achieve.
business_context_example: The team hit its target two weeks early.

definition: To produce worse results than expected.
business_context_example: The southern branch underperformed for two quarters running.

definition: A formal meeting to discuss an employee's work.
business_context_example: Performance reviews happen every June and December.

definition: The process of getting a new employee or client started.
business_context_example: Good onboarding cuts the time to first sale in half.

definition: A trial time at the start of a job.
business_context_example: The probation period is six months, then it's permanent.

definition: A document listing the duties of a role.
business_context_example: That task isn't in her job description, but she does it anyway.

definition: Money paid to an employee who is let go.
business_context_example: They offered three months' severance and a reference.

definition: Preparing people to take over key roles in future.
business_context_example: Succession planning matters most in a family business.

definition: The shared values and habits inside a company.
business_context_example: Corporate culture is what happens when the manager is away.

definition: A short public statement of a company's purpose.
business_context_example: Our mission statement fits in one sentence, on purpose.

definition: A big meeting where leaders update all staff and take questions.
business_context_example: The CEO announced the restructure at the town hall.

definition: To pass a problem to someone more senior.
business_context_example: If the client isn't happy by Friday, escalate it to me.

definition: Agreement and support from the people involved.
business_context_example: The plan is good, but we need buy-in from the regional heads.

definition: Official approval to go ahead.
business_context_example: We're waiting on sign-off from legal before we publish.

definition: The written record of what was said and decided in a meeting.
business_context_example: The minutes go out within 24 hours of every board meeting.

definition: The list of topics to be discussed in a meeting.
business_context_example: If it's not on the agenda, it waits until next time.

definition: To discuss in order to reach an agreement.
business_context_example: We negotiated a two-year deal instead of one.

definition: A different offer made in response to one you received.
business_context_example: Their counteroffer was 15% lower and we walked away.

definition: To finish a negotiation successfully.
business_context_example: He closed the deal on the phone in eleven minutes.

definition: An outcome where both sides benefit.
business_context_example: Shorter sessions and a lower price was a win-win.

definition: To leave a negotiation without an agreement.
business_context_example: Know your walk away price before the meeting starts.

definition: An advantage that gives you power in a negotiation.
business_context_example: Two other offers gave us leverage on the rent.

definition: A company that sells goods or services to you.
business_context_example: We reviewed four vendors before choosing the software.

definition: The process of buying goods and services for a company.
business_context_example: Procurement needs three quotes for anything over 5,000 euro.

definition: A formal offer to supply goods or services at a stated price.
business_context_example: We submitted a tender for the ministry's language programme.

definition: A contract defining the standard of service to be provided.
business_context_example: The service level agreement promises a reply within four hours.

definition: A mix of working from home and from the office.
business_context_example: Hybrid work here means two fixed days in the office.
